transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Johnson (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Sarah Lee (Nova Health - Head of Data), Daniel Park (Nova - ML Engineer), Priya Rao (Nova - Security Lead)
Links shared: pilot-results.xlsx, prompt-set-v2.csv, redwood-soc2.pdf (TBC), dedicated-latency-demo-notes.md

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. quick agenda — review the latest quality evals, talk through regressions we've seen on the new prompt set, and agree next steps. arjun, you'll kick off with the numbers?
[00:18] Arjun: yep, thanks maya. i pulled together the week-over-week results. we ran 500 prompts from the clinician-support set and compared outputs to the golden responses daniel shared. overall helpfulness score up slightly, but hallucination rate spiked on a subset of medication-summary prompts.
[00:35] Sarah: can you quantify the hallucination spike? like how many percent and on which prompts?
[00:42] Arjun: yeah, so baseline model (open-llm-13b) had hallucination ~4.8% on that set, whereas after prompt tuning and the new temperature we saw ~9.6% for certain free-text summarization prompts — mostly where patient history was long and multi-turn context got trimmed. we suspect kv cache mismatch and truncation pre-processing.
[01:05] Daniel: right, our prompts are longer because they include previous encounter notes. we noticed tokenization is sometimes different between our offline eval and the runtime. could be truncation heuristics.
[01:20] Maya: ok that's helpful. two threads here: one is model/runtime behavior (kv cache, prefix handling), other is prompt engineering and guardrails. arjun, what's the priority for the SE work?
[01:35] Arjun: i'd focus on reproducing the issue in a controlled benchmark first. run the exact prompt set with KV enabled and with KV disabled, measure latency, tokens, and hallucination rate. also try 8-bit quantized profile to see impact on hallucination. sometimes quantization affects generation slightly but reduces cost a lot.
[01:55] Sarah: our success criteria for the pilot is <5% hallucination on clinical summaries and median latency <350ms for 256-token outputs. cost target is also important but secondary to safety.
[02:10] Priya: and from security, we need audit logs for every request, SSO with SAML, KMS integration, and guaranteed data residency in-us. also SOC2 docs — you mentioned redwood-soc2 earlier.
[02:26] Maya: yes, i'll attach SOC2 and the network diagram after the call. redwood supports customer-managed KMS for private deployments and we can surface audit logs to your SIEM. for the hosted pilot we can enable strict retention and redaction policies.
[02:44] Daniel: regarding regression checks — we ran the new prompt set through the eval harness and flagged 32 regressions compared to last week's baseline. many were low-severity wording changes but 6 were high-severity (hallucinations or incorrect dosages).
[03:02] Arjun: for the high-severity ones we should add rule-based guardrails — basically a post-hoc verifier that checks for medication/dosage strings and falls back or flags for manual review. we can integrate a simple schema check as a stopgap.
[03:20] Sarah: that would help. can you sketch what the verifier would look like?
[03:28] Arjun: sure — a small microservice that receives the model output, runs regex/entity checks against a whitelist from your EHR, and if mismatch above threshold either returns a "needs human review" response or invokes a higher-fidelity model. it's cheap and quick to add.
[03:42] Maya: also, we can route high-risk prompts to Dedicated capacity with stricter model pins and KV cache tuning to reduce variance. that adds cost but gives more deterministic performance.
[03:55] Priya: cost tradeoffs aside, we need to know where logs live. do logs in hosted mode ever leave region? we need in-region logging and retention controls.
[04:06] Maya: hosted can be pinned to regions — with a Private deployment we can guarantee log residency. i'll confirm details in the SOC2/network diagram doc.
[04:20] Daniel: back to the evals — arjun, can you run a 5k prompt benchmark with KV enabled so we see distribution of latencies? our sample size was small this week.
[04:33] Arjun: yes, i'll spin that up. i'll run with three profiles: default hosted, hosted with KV/prefix caching, and an 8-bit quantized profile. collect latency P50/P95, token cost, and hallucination rate.
[04:45] Sarah: timeline?
[04:46] Arjun: target by next wednesday, 2026-04-07. i'll post results to the shared spreadsheet and annotate the prompts that triggered hallucinations.
[04:54] Maya: great — maya to-do is to send updated pricing that includes an optional Dedicated pilot with committed capacity and a one-week extension to the current pilot. also include the cost delta for the 8-bit quantized model.
[05:08] Daniel: one question — we saw slightly different token counts between your API and our local tokenizer. is there a recommended tokenizer or model artifact you prefer?
[05:18] Arjun: we recommend using the same model artifact and tokenizer we deploy; i'll share the exact tokenizer config. mismatch usually comes from whitespace normalization or unicode handling. we'll include a small script.
[05:30] Priya: on compliance, can Redwood support a private control plane so our security team can review everything before go-live?
[05:39] Maya: yes, Redwood Private offers a customer-managed control plane and can be deployed in your VPC. we usually spin that up for enterprise customers with strict residency and KMS requirements. it'll be in the optional SOW.
[05:52] Sarah: ok, sounds good. any blockers from our side? daniel - you said you'd finalize the prompt set — timeline?
[05:58] Daniel: i can finalize v2 of the prompt set and the golden answers by 2026-04-03. i want to add a few edge cases for long histories.
[06:07] Maya: perfect. let's talk about regression detection cadence — do you want an automated daily smoke check or weekly?
[06:14] Sarah: daily smoke checks with alerts for high-severity regressions would be ideal, weekly deeper analysis.
[06:21] Arjun: we can hook the eval harness to run a daily small-sample run and post to slack with detected regressions. high-sev goes to priority queue and triggers a canary rollback policy or fallback to a more conservative model.
[06:35] Maya: and we'll add a safety threshold — if hallucination over clinical summary >6% we automatically route to manual review or to the dedicated model. agreed?
[06:45] Sarah: agreed.
[06:47] Priya: one more item — vulnerability scanning of the private control plane images; we need scan reports.
[06:54] Maya: noted. i'll pass that to our security team and they'll share the SBOM and vulnerability scan cadence.
[07:02] Arjun: small note — the 8-bit quantized profile sometimes nudges wording; to make sure we don't degrade clinical accuracy we'll run the quantized model against the golden set and compute a clinical-accuracy metric in addition to BLEU/ROUGE — something more task-specific.
[07:18] Daniel: what metric are you thinking?
[07:21] Arjun: a simple label-based accuracy where we extract key clinical facts (diagnosis, medication, dosage) and compare to gold. compute F1 on those entities. that'll surface hallucinations that matter.
[07:34] Sarah: that sounds right. let's make sure the extractor is aligned with our EHR fields.
[07:40] Arjun: i'll coordinate with daniel on the extractor schema.
[07:44] Maya: ok, recap and owners: arjun runs the 5k benchmark and extractor tests (due 4/7); daniel finalizes prompts and gold answers (due 4/3); priya to send SOC2 preference & KMS vendor (due 4/5); maya sends pricing and SOW with dedicated option (due 4/2). we'll reconvene next week same time. any final questions?
[08:10] Sarah: none from me, thanks.
[08:12] Daniel: nope, thanks everyone.
[08:14] Priya: thanks.
[08:15] Maya: thanks all, i'll share notes and the files after the call. bye.

Notes on transcript quality: minor transcription artifacts noted — product names sometimes mis-capitalized (e.g., "kv-cache" vs "KV cache"), some agent names labelled generically in the raw tool export. The substantive technical details were captured and action owners confirmed.
